title: Inference budget playbook & KV demo - Echo Labs scoping
summary: Redwood team walked through an Optimize playbook focused on batching, sessionization, and prefix (KV) caching. Discussed expected cost savings for Echo Labs' chat use case, latency SLOs, and pilot scope. Action: share cost-simulator, security appendix, and schedule 1-week trial with sample traffic.
action_items: Samir - Share cost-simulator spreadsheet and simplified playbook - due 2026-06-12
Jules - Provide suggested model + quantization profiles for Echo's 2 tokens/sec baseline - due 2026-06-15
Maya - Upload 48h sample request traces to shared bucket for sim runs - due 2026-06-14
next_steps: Samir to send pricing & simulator link
Echo Labs to provide sample traces and SLA targets
questions: What is the minimum cache TTL you recommend for sessionized chat?
Can Redwood run the sim against our production traffic snapshot?
How does Dedicated change the economics vs hosted for small bursty workloads?
transcript:
Header: Date: Jun 10 2026 | Start: 4:00 PM PDT | Duration: ~62 min
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jules Rivera (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Echo Labs - Head ML), Roberto Diaz (Echo Labs - Infra), Asha Patel (Echo Labs - Product)
Links shared: https://redwood.example.com/optimize-playbook (deck), https://s3.example.com/echo-sample-traces (sample traces placeholder), cost-sim: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/cost-simulator

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I see we have Maya, Roberto and Asha from Echo Labs. Quick intro, I'm Samir, AE on the Optimize team, and Jules is our SE. We'll run through a lightweight playbook for batching, sessionization and prefix KV caching and then talk pilot scope.
[00:22] Maya: Hi all, yep thanks. We're mostly worried about token cost ramp as user growth hits us. Latency target for chat is around 200 ms p95 if possible, but we can tolerate up to 350 for some flows.
[00:36] Jules: Got it. I'll call out tradeoffs: batching and concurrency reduce unit cost but increase tail latency; KV/prefix cache dramatically helps for sessionized flows if hit rates are high.
[00:50] Roberto: Quick note, we run on multi-cloud right now, and any private deployment needs to sit inside our VPC, SSO to Okta, and we need SOC2 plus an audit trail.
[01:05] Samir: That's standard; Redwood Private supports VPC and we can map to your KMS. We'll include our SOC 2 appendix.
[01:18] Asha: For context, our median prompt length is short, ~40 tokens, replies average 120 tokens. Sessions are sticky per user, and we suspect ~70% of subsequent requests share common prefixes.
[01:33] Jules: That prefix stat is great — high prefix overlap is where KV caching shines. If we can get a 60-70% hit rate on prefix cache, you can see order-of-magnitude token savings for long threads.
[01:47] Maya: Could you show the cost sim with those numbers?
[01:51] Samir: Sure, I'm going to share the sim. (link posted) This is a conservative sim we run: input tokens, output tokens, sessionization window, cache hit probability, batching latency profile.
[02:08] Jules: I'll walk the rough math — assume baseline: no batching, no cache; 1.8M tokens/day at current traffic. With a 65% KV hit and light batching (batch size avg 6), we get roughly 45% token cost reduction in the sim here.
[02:28] Roberto: Is that taking into account KV cache replication cost? We have cross-AZ requirements.
[02:33] Jules: The sim includes a small fixed cost for the cache layer and replication but it's minor vs token savings. Note though cold-starts and new sessions still pay full token price.
[02:46] Samir: Also worth calling out session affinity. If you can affinity requests to the same serving pool, cache locality improves and latency improves too.
[02:56] Maya: How does affinity affect autoscaling? We see big spikes during product releases.
[03:02] Jules: Affinity helps per-session, but for spikes we'd suggest a hybrid: reserved Dedicated pool for baseline plus hosted burst capacity, or autoscale policies tuned in Redwood Dedicated. That gives predictability for steady traffic and elasticity for spikes.
[03:20] Asha: Any red flags we should watch for when enabling KV prefix cache?
[03:24] Jules: A few: noisy prefixes reducing hit rate, very short sessions where cache warms slowly, and hallucination risk if you naively reuse cached outputs without versioning. We recommend version pins and a short TTL with validation checks.
[03:39] Maya: You mentioned TTL — what do you recommend?
[03:42] Jules: For chat threads, 10-30 minutes TTL usually balances freshness and reuse. For high-security or high-change contexts, we lower TTL and accept lower hit rate.
[03:54] Samir: I'll flag that in the playbook. We have a small decision table in the deck for TTL by use-case.
[03:59] (short crosstalk)
[04:10] Roberto: On the infra side, how do you handle KV storage? Is it in-memory on the GPU node, or an external Redis?
[04:17] Jules: Redwood's runtime supports a local KV cache per serving instance for ultra-low latency, and an optional external tier (Redis or equivalent) for larger working sets. Local KV gives best latency but needs session affinity. External KV reduces affinity requirements but adds ms-level latency.
[04:36] Maya: Suppose we want to prioritize latency for our VIP users and cost for the rest — can policies be per-route?
[04:43] Samir: Yes, you can define per-route policies in the Console — route-level batching, cache TTL, fallback models. That way VIP traffic hits low-latency config, and non-VIP gets more aggressive batching/quantization.
[04:59] Asha: About quantization — you hinted at model + quantization recs earlier. Can you summarize what you'd recommend for our workloads?
[05:06] Jules: For short prompts and ~120 token outputs, 4-bit quantized variants of the same base model often work well. We'll provide a recommended profile set: baseline fp16 for best quality, q4 for cost sensitive routes, and a fallback smaller model for ultra-cheap. We'll also show quality delta sim results.
[05:26] Maya: How do you measure 'quality delta'? Human eval or automatic metrics?
[05:30] Jules: Both; we run automated BLEU/ROUGE-ish checks plus a small human eval for sensitive flows. We attach those to regression alerts in Redwood Optimize.
[05:41] Samir: Let's jump into a quick live sim with your numbers — Jules, take it away.
[05:48] Jules: Alright I'm switching to the sim spreadsheet. (slight noise) The left column is your traffic snapshot; I set sessionization window at 20 minutes initially and cache hit at 0.65 per Asha's estimate. Note the bucket for cold-start ratio is 12%.
[06:09] Maya: Where does cold-start come from? New users only?
[06:12] Jules: New sessions and sessions that have expired TTL. Also when route model changes or cache invalidations happen.
[06:20] Roberto: The sim shows 47% cost reduction and 23% higher p95 latency in some batching configs — does that align with your real-world benchmarks?
[06:29] Jules: Yes that delta is expected. But with per-route priority and local KV for sticky sessions, you can recover most of the latency hit for important flows. Also concurrency tuning helps.
[06:44] Asha: Can Redwood run the sim with our actual traces? We can upload a 48h sample.
[06:49] Samir: Absolutely — that will tighten the sim. I'll put that as an action item.
[06:54] (spotty audio for a few seconds)
[07:10] Maya: Security check — we need to know where logs go, retention and whether we can disable request logging for PII routes.
[07:18] Samir: You can configure audit log retention per-route and disable full request logging; redaction hooks are available plus integration with customer KMS for storing keys. We'll include the security appendix and a short note on PII redaction patterns.
[07:37] Roberto: Do you support customer-managed keys (CMKs) and HSM?
[07:40] Jules: Yes, KMS integrations and HSM are supported in Private deployments. For hosted we offer envelope encryption with optional CMK bring-your-own-key for some plans.
[07:54] Asha: Pricing — can you give high level numbers for hosted vs dedicated?
[07:58] Samir: High level: hosted per-token pricing with volume tiers; Dedicated is committed monthly capacity with lower per-token marginal cost and more predictable latency. Exact figures I'll send in the follow-up quote — depends on reservation size and model family.
[08:13] Maya: If we do a small pilot, what's a reasonable commitment?
[08:16] Samir: For pilots we usually start with a 2-week trial with sample capacity (no long-term commit). For Dedicated we can do a month-long evaluation and scale to a quarterly trial.
[08:28] Jules: Also request routing: during pilot we'll set conservative batching to avoid p95 spikes. Then as we validate quality, we push more aggressive batching.
[08:38] Asha: Let's talk success criteria — what should we measure in the pilot?
[08:42] Jules: I'd suggest: token cost delta vs baseline, p50/p95 latency, KV hit rate, error rate and quality regressions on a small eval set.
[08:52] Maya: For quality regressions, can Redwood alert us automatically?
[08:55] Samir: Yes, Optimize supports regression alerts tied to prompt sets and thresholds; we can wire alerts to your Slack or PagerDuty.
[09:05] (longer section of sim walkthrough, timestamps jump)
[15:12] Jules: I'm toggling model variants — see how q4 reduces tokens by 18% but shows a small quality delta on the 'summarize' prompt. We mark that with a tag so you can roll back.
[20:30] Asha: A few practical ops questions: how do you version the cache so we don't serve stale completions after a model patch?
[20:36] Jules: Cache versioning is handled by model-version + route tag; invalidations can be done via API when you push new model versions. We also support automatic cascaded invalidation on canary rollouts.
[20:49] Maya: One more on privacy — can we avoid sending user identifiers to Redwood? We prefer hashing locally.
[20:55] Samir: You can hash/anonymize on your side; Redwood doesn't require PII and supports hashed user IDs for affinity.
[21:03] Roberto: On the infra network side: can Redwood agents deploy inside our VPC and speak to our Redis?
[21:09] Jules: Yes, Private supports in-VPC connectors and we can partner with your infra team on network policies. We'll provide a runbook for peering and subnets.
[21:21] Maya: This is great. Any limitations on sequence length? Our use sometimes spikes to 2k tokens in longer context.
[21:28] Jules: Runtime supports up to model limits; the cost sim can model longer sequences but batching behavior changes. Long sequences reduce effective batch size because of memory constraints, so economics shift — we'll mark that in the sim report.
[21:43] Asha: Could you walk alternatives? If we decide to avoid prefix cache for now and just rely on batching and quant, what savings might we see?
[21:50] Jules: In many short-session apps batching+quantization gets you 20-35% savings. Adding a 50% prefix hit can push that to ~50% or more. It's incremental but meaningful.
[22:05] Samir: To recap next steps: Samir shares sim & security appendix; Echo uploads traces; Jules runs sim and returns a tuned playbook; then pilot kickoff.
[22:18] Maya: That works. One ask — can the playbook include a quick checklist for Prod ops?
[22:23] Samir: Yep we'll add a 1-page ops checklist with runbook snippets.
[22:28] Asha: Anything else on ownership of action items?
[22:31] Samir: We'll capture and send a short follow-up email.
[22:35] (wrap up)
[22:40] Samir: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up by Friday with the sim sheet and security docs.
[22:46] Maya: Thanks, talk soon.
[22:48] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-hearings, background noise during the upload discussion, and minor speaker label inconsistencies.
